newsitem.title: JAPAN: Red Cross sets up medical clinic at hostage site.
newsitem.headline: Red Cross sets up medical clinic at hostage site.

text.p: Japan's Foreign Ministry said on Tuesday that the Red Cross had set up a clinic in the Japanese ambassador's residence in the Peruvian capital Lima to give medical care to 140 hostages.

"We confirmed with Red Cross staff in Lima that there is a medical room inside of the ambassador's residence and medical care is going to be available 24 hours a day to the hostages," a ministry spokesman told reporters.

The spokesman had no details on what equipment was in the clinic and if Red Cross doctors would staff the unit to give instant help to hostages held by guerrillas of the Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA).
The spokesman quoted a Red Cross official who was recently in the residence as saying the hostages looked tired but no captive at this stage needed any special medical care.
MRTA guerrillas stormed the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima last Tuesday during a reception to mark Emperor Akihito's birthday, taking more than 500 hostages.
After freeing a large number of captives, the rebels still hold dozens of top Peruvian government officials and about 30 high-ranking Japanese businessmen and diplomats.
